A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical work, with the same authors, main characterization, and learning rule. All 14 pages of each version, including Appendices A.1–A.7 and their equations, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports mathematical constructions, counterexamples, and proofs, but no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes. Its random-bit constructions are theoretical arguments.

after.justification: v3 remains entirely theoretical, including its appendices. The revised probabilistic guarantees are mathematical results, not empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Section 6 retains the same learning rule: split the sample, simulate a winning game strategy, construct bounded-label cells, and apply MedNet within cells. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Neither version uses training or evaluation datasets. The theoretical instance spaces, label spaces, and hypothesis-class examples are retained.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. MedNet remains a component of the theoretical learner, rather than an experimentally compared baseline.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an empirical evaluation protocol. The theoretical sampling and sample-splitting constructions are unchanged.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablation, sensitivity, or robustness experiments. The appendix examples and counterexample constructions are retained; the revised mathematical conclusions are addressed under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Replacing an expected-risk guarantee with an almost-sure guarantee concerns theorems, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Neither version reports empirical scores, rankings, or measured qualitative findings. The changes to formal risk guarantees are theoretical revisions assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Theorem 5.1 changes from infinite expected risk at every sample size to infinite risk almost surely at every sample size. Section 3 and the final Fubini conclusions in Appendices A.6–A.7 are revised accordingly. This is a limited formal strengthening: v1 already contained the almost-sure divergence argument, while the constructions, assumptions, main characterization, and upper-bound proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction now explicitly claims almost-sure infinite risk for every sample size, replacing its infinite-expected-risk claim. The central characterization of realizable learnability and the constructive upper-bound contribution retain their scope.

C2.justification: The rare-event mechanism, qualifications about constructivity and compactness, and barriers to agnostic learning are unchanged. The new Impact Statement gives a generic assessment of theoretical relevance and societal impact without adding a specific scientific limitation.

D1.justification: The algorithmic specification in Section 6.5 and constructivity discussion in Appendix A.2 are unchanged. Neither version adds implementation settings, hardware information, or code/data access resources.

R1.justification: The cited research and substantive positioning are unchanged. Several references receive publication metadata, and Bousquet et al. gains separate 2020 extended-version and 2021 conference entries explicitly identified as versions of the same work.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized edits to the lower-bound statements and proof endings, adds an Impact Statement, and updates bibliographic wording and citation years. The narrative and section organization otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Both versions retain the two-column format and contain no figures or tables. The Impact Statement and expanded reference entries move the references' start from page 8 to page 9 and shift appendix text and equations across columns and pages.

improvement.justification: v3 aligns the introduction, Theorem 5.1, and appendix conclusions with the almost-sure infinite-risk argument already present in v1. This improves logical precision because infinite expected risk alone does not rule out almost-sure consistency. The gain is limited: the underlying proof strategy, main characterization, learner, and limitations are unchanged.
